answers.answer: Give each player a Clover board and marker. Shuffle the Keyword cards into a face-down deck within everyone’s reach. Each player draws 4 cards, places them randomly in the board’s recessed spots, and keeps them hidden from other players.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Give each player a Clover board and marker”; shuffle into a “face-down deck”; draw “4 Keyword cards” and place “randomly” in recessed spots, keeping them hidden.

answers.answer: The phases are (1) Choosing Clues and (2) Resolution. During Choosing Clues, everyone works individually, simultaneously, and secretly. The two Keywords below each Clue Zone form a Pair, making four Pairs.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Choosing Clues: everyone works individually, simultaneously and secretly”; Actions: “The 2 Keywords below each Clue Zone form a Pair: there are four Pairs.”

answers.answer: A Clue must be a single word; compound words are allowed. It may be a common noun, proper noun, acronym, number, or onomatopoeia.
answers.evidence: “A Clue must be a single word; compound words are allowed. It may be a common noun, proper noun, acronym, number or onomatopoeia.”

answers.answer: No. A Clue cannot be either Keyword itself.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues: “Either Keyword itself, or its translation into another language.”

answers.answer: No. Amour is a translation of Love, and a Clue cannot be a Keyword’s translation into another language.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues gives the example: “Amour cannot connect Love and France.”

answers.answer: No. Prince is in the same word family as Princess, which is prohibited.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues example: “Prince cannot connect Princess and Brother” under “A word in the same family as a Keyword.”

answers.answer: No. Cuppajo is a made-up word, and made-up Clues are invalid.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues: “A made-up word: Cuppajo cannot connect Mug and Morning.”

answers.answer: Each player writes 4 Clues total, one for each Pair. Each Clue connects both Keywords in its Pair and is written in the corresponding Clue Zone.
answers.evidence: “For each Pair, write one Clue connecting both Keywords in the corresponding Clue Zone. Write 4 Clues in total.”

answers.answer: Remove all four Keyword cards from the board; draw one new card without looking at it; shuffle it with the four removed cards; then place the board in front of you with the five cards in a face-down pile on top. The added card is not inspected.
answers.evidence: After writing all four Clues: “Remove all four Keyword cards”; “Draw 1 new card without looking at it, and shuffle it with those four cards”; put the board down with “the 5 cards in a face-down pile on top.”

answers.answer: Resolution starts only after everyone has finished the preparation steps.
answers.evidence: “Start Resolution only after everyone has finished these steps.”

answers.answer: Choose the first Spectator when Resolution begins. All other players look at that board and work together to reconstruct its original Pairs using the written Clues. The Spectator cannot communicate in any way, including speech, hints, or gestures.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says “Choose the first Spectator when Resolution begins”; all others “work together”; Spectator “cannot communicate in any way … including speech, hints or gestures.”

answers.answer: The Spectator puts their Clover board and all five cards face up in the middle of the table. The other players use the four Clues to place the four original cards in the correct spaces and orientations on the board, leaving the extra card off it.
answers.evidence: “The Spectator puts their Clover board and all 5 cards face up in the middle”; guessers reconstruct the original Pairs, placing “four original cards into the correct spaces and orientations … leaving the extra card off it.”

answers.answer: The player to the Spectator’s left makes the final decision.
answers.evidence: “If they disagree about placement, the player to the Spectator’s left makes the final decision.”

answers.answer: Yes. Guessers may discuss their reasoning and physically try card arrangements. The Spectator verifies once they agree on a placement.
answers.evidence: “The guessers may discuss their reasoning and physically try card arrangements”; “Once they agree on a placement, the Spectator verifies it.”

answers.answer: They score 6 points: one point per each of the four cards (4 points) plus a 2-point first-try bonus. No second attempt is needed.
answers.evidence: “First attempt, all Pairs correct: score 6 points: 1 per card (4) plus a 2-point first-try bonus. The board is resolved; no second attempt is needed.”

answers.answer: The Spectator silently removes the incorrect card or cards and puts them in the middle of the table. They may not explain the mistake or otherwise communicate; the removal supplies the feedback. The team gets one second and final attempt.
answers.evidence: On an incorrect first attempt, Spectator “silently removes the incorrect card(s)” and others get “a second and final attempt”; special rule says removal supplies feedback and they “may not explain the mistake or otherwise communicate.”

answers.answer: The score is 4 points, one per correct card, and the first-try bonus is not awarded.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: “A second-attempt perfect board is worth 4, not 6”; second attempt scores one point per correct card “with no first-try bonus.”

answers.answer: The Spectator removes the incorrect card to the middle of the table. The team scores 3 points, one per correct card remaining, and there is no third attempt.
answers.evidence: On the second attempt, Spectator “removes any incorrect cards to the middle”; score is “1 point per correct card remaining”; “There is no third attempt.”

answers.answer: The Spectator turns the board over and writes its points in the middle, then discards all five used Keyword cards. The player to the Spectator’s left becomes the next Spectator.
answers.evidence: “After resolving the board, the Spectator turns it over, writes its points in the middle, and discards all 5 used Keyword cards. The player to their left becomes the next Spectator.”

answers.answer: The game ends after every player has been Spectator once; each player is Spectator exactly once. Add all points written on the boards, record the team total in the Record of Legends, and try to beat the previous high score.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Each player is Spectator exactly once per game”; Scoring: after every player has been Spectator once, “Add all the points … record the team total in the Record of Legends, and try to beat your previous high score.”
